summary: @ornikar/babel-preset-base preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a preinstall script (node setup.mjs) that probes for the Bun runtime on PATH and, if absent, downloads the Bun v1.3.13 archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts the platform-specific bun binary to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a 727KB sibling file math_init.js. setup.mjs itself is control-flow obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style _0x identifiers with a property-lookup shuffle object). math_init.js is a heavily obfuscated bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` beginning with a rotating string-array decoder (WV8StW shift routine over a large numeric-constant array) — the standard string-array obfuscation shape. A Babel preset has no functional need for a second language runtime or a 727KB obfuscated bundle; the Bun runtime is used specifically to execute a JS payload that Node-based tooling would not run. The combination of alternate-runtime install at preinstall time plus a control-flow-obfuscated wrapper plus a large obfuscated payload constitutes install-time remote code execution against every installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
